claims.text: The target alloys are solid solutions containing at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 at.% each.
In single-phase, chemically disordered BCC HEAs, superconducting behavior is governed primarily by overall valence electron count.
Overall valence electron count governs superconductivity through the averaged density of states at the Fermi level.
High configurational disorder preserves isotropic s-wave electron-phonon coupling.
The Nb-Ta-Hf-Zr-Ti-based baseline has an ambient-pressure superconducting transition near 7–8 K.
The proposed Nb-Ta-Hf-Zr-Ti-based baseline is a single-phase disordered BCC solid solution.
The baseline retains a zero-resistance superconducting state to approximately 190.6 GPa.
The superconducting transition temperature remains nearly invariant under high pressure.
Substitution by an element of different valence can shift overall VEC while retaining a homogeneous, disordered BCC phase.
Configurational disorder averages out local bonding variations.
A disordered BCC lattice supports an isotropic electronic structure conducive to uniform s-wave pairing.
VEC sets the Fermi-level density of states, which optimizes the electron-phonon coupling required for BCS superconductivity.
Configurational disorder prevents local chemical ordering or phase separation and thereby stabilizes superconductivity.
Tuning VEC closer to an optimum will increase Tc or make Tc more robust.
VEC-optimized variants will retain a zero-resistance superconducting state under high pressure.
A significant deviation from the optimum VEC will decrease Tc, broaden the transition, or suppress superconductivity.
Chemical ordering or phase separation will decrease Tc, broaden the superconducting transition, or suppress superconductivity.
Once ordering or phase separation occurs, interface effects and other factors make the proposed VEC-disorder mechanism non-predictive.
Existing studies qualitatively support a relationship between disorder and superconducting Tc in BCC Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti HEAs.
Existing studies qualitatively support a relationship between VEC and Tc in the proposed alloy system.
